facts.content: Patient has a sudden severe headache since this morning.
facts.source_text: CC: Sudden severe HA since this morning

facts.content: Onset of headache was approximately 4 hours ago, unilateral and left-sided behind the eye.
facts.source_text: Onset ~4h ago; unilateral L-sided, behind eye unclear

facts.content: The headache intensity is about 6 out of 10.
facts.source_text: intensity ~6/10

facts.content: Associated symptoms include blurred vision with zigzag lines, dizziness, photophobia, and nausea with vomiting twice.
facts.source_text: assoc blurred vision with zigzag lines (visual aura), dizziness, photophobia/screen intolerance, N/V x2

facts.content: Symptoms worsen with movement.
facts.source_text: worse with movement

facts.content: Paracetamol taken roughly 3 hours ago provided no relief.
facts.source_text: paracetamol ~3h ago no relief

facts.content: No focal weakness or gait abnormalities.
facts.source_text: no focal weakness; gait OK

facts.content: Patient has a history of prior kidney stones.
facts.source_text: PMH: Prior kidney stones

facts.content: Mother has migraines.
facts.source_text: Mother migraines

facts.content: Family history of hypothyroidism.
facts.source_text: hypothyroidism in family

facts.content: Patient does not take any regular medications.
facts.source_text: Meds: None regular

facts.content: Patient has no known drug allergies.
facts.source_text: Allergies: NKDA (pt not aware of any)

facts.content: Pregnancy is unlikely.
facts.source_text: SH: Pregnancy unlikely

facts.content: Diagnosed with an acute migraine with aura, first episode, characterized by left-sided headache with visual aura, nausea, vomiting, and photophobia.
facts.source_text: 1) Acute migraine with aura—first episode; L-sided HA with visual aura, N/V, photophobia

facts.content: No focal neurological symptoms, red flags partially absent, but new severe headache warrants in-person evaluation.
facts.source_text: no focal neuro sx; partial red flags absent but new severe HA warrants in-person eval

facts.content: Patient experiences health anxiety with concerns about tumors and strokes.
facts.source_text: 2) Health anxiety—concerns about tumor/stroke

facts.content: Prescribed trial of ibuprofen with food, an antiemetic from pharmacy, and oral fluids including a sugary carbonated drink.
facts.source_text: Migraine abortive: Trial ibuprofen (with food) + antiemetic (from pharmacy) + oral fluids incl sugary carbonated drink as advised

facts.content: Advised to escalate care if there is no improvement, worsening symptoms, new neurological deficits, confusion, or neck stiffness.
facts.source_text: Escalation: If no improvement or worsening (severe/progressive HA, persistent vomiting, new neuro deficits, confusion, neck stiffness), attend urgent care/A&E

facts.content: Same-day in-person neurological exam appointment arranged; to be canceled if symptoms fully resolve.
facts.source_text: Follow-up: Same-day in-person neuro exam appointment arranged; cancel if fully resolved

facts.content: Patient educated on typical migraine course and advised to avoid screens, bright light, and triggers and to rest.
facts.source_text: Education: Typical migraine course (4–72h possible); avoid screen/bright light; rest; avoid triggers

facts.content: Patient advised to return if pregnancy is suspected or if headache becomes severe, presents with thunderclap onset, fever or rash, or new neurological symptoms appear.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: Return if pregnancy suspected or HA becomes “worst ever,” thunderclap onset, fever/rash, or new neuro symptoms
